scenes.onScreen: "Safe reads and loops": three numbered lines (1. get(key, default) never raises an error; 2. items() gives key and value together; 3. keys() and values() give one side each) and an analogy card: walking along the price board: you can read the names, the prices, or both together

scenes.narration: Four methods cover most dictionary work. Get reads a key, and gives a default if the key is missing, so no error. Items gives key and value pairs together. Keys gives the keys. Values gives the values. Think of walking along the price board. You can read the names, the prices, or both together. A for loop over a dictionary walks over its keys by default.

scenes.narration: [HL 1] A dictionary with two fish. [HL 2] Get with a key that exists gives its value, five hundred. [HL 3] Get with a missing key gives the default we choose. Zero. No error. [HL 4] Items gives each pair. We unpack them into fish and price. [HL 5] Print each pair. [HL 6] Keys gives the keys, and list turns them into a list. [HL 7] Values does the same for the values.

code.source:
prices = {"pomfret": 350, "prawns": 500}
print(prices.get("prawns"))
print(prices.get("crab", 0))
for fish, price in prices.items():
    print(fish, price)
print(list(prices.keys()))
print(list(prices.values()))

scenes.narration: Here is a useful detail. Prices is one dictionary object. The methods keys, values and items do not copy it. They give a live view of the same dictionary. We wrapped them in list to get a plain list to print. If you change the dictionary, the view changes too. That also explains the bug of the day.

scenes.narration: Let us recap. One: get returns a default instead of raising a KeyError. Two: items gives key and value together, keys and values give one side. Three: A plain for loop over a dictionary walks over its keys. Four: Do not add or remove keys while looping over a dictionary. Pause the video, and say these ideas out loud, once, slowly.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: changing a dictionary while looping
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We add a new key while looping over the dictionary. Python says, runtime error, dictionary changed size during iteration. Python cannot walk a dictionary that keeps growing. Loop over a list of the keys instead. That list is a snapshot, so you are free to change the dictionary itself.

props.error:
File "loopdict.py", line 2, in <module>
    for fish in prices:

RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration

lines: RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration

props.why: Adding or removing keys while looping changes the size of the dictionary being walked, so Python stops with a RuntimeError; loop over a list copy of the keys instead.

shorts.title: Safe reads with get
shorts.hook: "The get method reads a key safely."
shorts.script: The get method reads a key safely. Prices dot get, crab, comma, zero. If crab exists, you get its value. If not, you get the default, zero, and no error. It is shorter than checking with in, and it is easy to read. Use get whenever a missing key is a normal case, and not a mistake in your program. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: No more key errors.

shorts.title: Items
shorts.hook: "To walk through every pair, loop over items."
shorts.script: To walk through every pair, loop over items. For fish, comma, price, in prices dot items. Each round gives you a key and its value together, already unpacked into two names. Print them, add them, compare them, whatever you need. It is the standard way to loop over a dictionary, and it reads almost like English. Try it today. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Keys and values together.

shorts.title: Keys and values
shorts.script: Sometimes you only need one side. Keys gives the names. Values gives the prices. Loop over values to add up all the prices, without caring about the fish names. A plain for loop over a dictionary gives its keys. So for fish in prices is the same as for fish in prices dot keys. Pick the shortest form that reads well. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: One side at a time.

shorts.title: Changed size
shorts.script: The loop bug for dictionaries. You add a key while looping over the dictionary. Python says, runtime error, dictionary changed size during iteration. It cannot walk something that keeps growing. The fix is to loop over a list of the keys instead. That list is a snapshot, so you can change the real dictionary safely inside the loop. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Loop over a snapshot.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.script: Why did the dictionary love loops? It could finally read every entry. Your challenge. Make a dictionary of marks, maths eighty, science ninety, english seventy. Print the total of the marks with a loop over the values. You should get two hundred forty. Then try printing each subject with its mark, using items. Share your code in the comments. Keep coding, says Xecxec! Full video: EP 34.
